241.t: His father Peter Valentine and the reserve brass bands
241.s: His father played alto and other horns in the Pickwick band; the father is still living, over seventy, and a later interview is mooted.
241.q: Yeah, both reserve bands. Well first of all, what was your father's name? Peter Valdeman. Peter. He's not living is he? Yeah he's living. Well that's what I wondered. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

724.t: Brother Paul, his father and relatives who played music
724.s: He played with his brother, who had a little piano and drums; his father painted and owned a mandolin but no one else played.
724.q: I'm back to your brother. Did he play with bands ever? No. He had started out on drums. He just played a few jobs. He'd keep them all. What was his name? Paul. Paul Garland.

251.t: Father the cigar maker and singer; musical uncles
251.s: Albert's father was a cigar maker with a great voice, and several uncles played music. He names uncle Wilson, a cornetist killed after a job, and Naval, who died of tuberculosis.
251.q: He was a cigar maker by trade. My daddy traveled to various parts of the country making cigars familiar. But he also had a great voice. And my grandfather's son, my grandmother sang also. I had a lot of uncles who played music.

41.t: Father the trumpeter, brother Vic, French family name, sister
41.s: His father played trumpet, brother Vic played tenor, the family name is French (father born near Paris), and his sister played piano.
41.q: Well, no, he played the Tokyo Gardens out at West End at concerts and stuff. And then my brother Vic, who's two years younger than myself, was a real good tenor man. He took up tenor. In fact, he's got lessons from Skag and Leon. Skag was one of good clarinet players and saxophone men in the late…

968.t: Brother Simon's brass band playing and the Frazier relatives
968.s: Simon played bass drum and sousaphone in brass bands, and Lawrence followed him; an uncle was a piano tuner and a cousin a piano player.
968.q: Yeah, he did play that in brass band and, uh, he also played bass drum. That's why I took it up behind him.

44.s: Parents, brothers and sisters of Maxey played violin, guitar and piano; fifteen children.
44.q: Well, my mother was a violin player. My mother was a violin player. My daddy also. And I have two brothers who are violin players. And myself, my brother was a father and a family to play. Most of the rest of the play guitar. Get the piano. What about your sister? She was a piano player.

972.s: His father made and played a homemade flute, played informally with friends and serenaded birthdays; Pavageau was in Columbia when his father died in 1933.
972.q: My father used to play the carnage. Oh. Yeah, but my father was most, then from a carnage he was a seagull maker, you know what I mean, in New Orleans, you see. And then he took a fishing pole and made a flute out of it, it blew.

841.t: Harris's father, a clarinet and saxophone player, and his band photograph
841.s: Harris says his father played with name bands; a picture on the wall is taken down to look at.
841.q: Well, the regular band, they had a band of the old, I don't even know the name of it. That's part of the band there. I don't really know. Oh, that's a picture over there.

192.t: Father's guitar, mattress making, and brother Sam the drummer
192.s: His father played guitar and made mattresses; oldest brother Sam was a drummer who no longer plays.
192.q: My father played guitar years back in the old-own Seminard Parish. The old guitar player, but he left and his main occupation was mattress making, self-employed.

537.t: Father back in New Orleans and brother John's trumpet playing
537.s: His father played with Paul Barbarin and met his mother practising with her brother Lester; Wendell grew up hearing his brother John and sat in with Olympia Brass Band.
537.q: Yeah he played a lot with like Paul Barbarin, Uncle Lester Santiago played piano in the band, and when my dad first came back, my uncle was like, “Man you’d better learn to play some of this music.” And my dad wasn’t playing traditional music at all. So he and my uncle Lester used to practice…

491.t: The Bryant brothers: Ray and Tom, young prodigies, and sister Vera
491.s: Ray and Tom Bryant played with grown-ups while in school; Golson describes their talent and sister Vera, mother of Kevin Eubanks.
491.q: Tom Bryant. Yeah, he was the same. I think they were – Ray was 14 when I met them. Tom was 15. These guys, they were exceptional. That’s all I can say. They were exceptional. So as a result, they played with the grownups, I guess you would call them – guys 35, 40 years old. We called them the old…

953.t: Where the musical ability came from: father, grandfather and genetics
953.s: He speculates about his father's clarinet and a singing grandfather, and argues that musical talent is genetic rather than environmental.
953.q: Well, that’s very interesting. I–my father told me that he played clarinet at one time. I never heard him play clarinet. I have the feeling it wasn’t something he was doing regularly, you know. I never heard him play, and so I don’t know. But other than that uh I think it’s probably uh further…
